title: Effects of mask wearing on exhaled human particle formation
summary: During the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, various types of masks were used. They were intended to prevent the transmission of potentially infectious aerosols. In this study, we measure the exhaled particles while the participant rides a stationary bicycle and wears different masks.
conditions: Acute infections of the upper and lower respiratory tract caused by airborne pathogens

interventions.name: 50 healthy probants are exercised on an ergometer. They wear different masks during the task. Particle emission is measured  as particle concentration in a sealed measuring chamber.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Legal age
• Consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
• Chronic respiratory diseases (e.g., non-seasonal asthma, COPD)
• Acute symptomatic respiratory infections
• Physically debilitating heart disease (coronary heart disease, heart failure, cardiac arrhythmia)
• Other physically debilitating conditions, such as renal insufficiency, immunosuppression, or neurological deficits
• Smoking
